title: Guided process tour of the Interactive PFD
label: audit:pfd

basis.drawing: frontend/index.html, inline svg#pfd-svg, viewBox 0 0 2070 1000; units are g.unit[data-unit], streams are g.st[data-stream] holding path.cas and path.core (S16 holds path.vent)
basis.live_reply: solve reply at the registry defaults, captured in headless Chrome from a site built into the scratch folder (wasm built with CARGO_TARGET_DIR in the scratch cargo folder). Saved at stagef/uiux/audit_pfd/capture/reply_default.json, with the registry at capture/registry.json and ten variant replies at audit_pfd/variants/

conventions.path_notation: reply paths use the data-bind convention of app.js bound() and panels.js walk(): inside an array a name that is not an index picks the entry whose id equals it, and an object with a value field yields that value. So units.htgr.conditions.ROT.value and balances.energy.ihx_duty.value both resolve. Train profile points carry a stream key and no id, so they are addressed by index, with the stream named beside it. Flags carry a param key and no id, so they are found by param in code.
conventions.token: where given, token is a {{path|decimals}} string that panels.js fillText() already resolves, so a caption can be filled with the existing helper

sources.reply: the live solve reply (state.lastOk); follows the controls
sources.streams_json: data/streams.json, rows of run FS_B_REC_F from results/Integrated_Mass_Balance.csv; precomputed at the headline basis, does not follow the controls
sources.results_csv: data/csv/<file>, the shipped results CSVs; precomputed, does not follow the controls

follows_controls.yes: live calculation of the anchored port; moves with the controls
follows_controls.fixed: registry constant shown by the reply; never moves
follows_controls.scenario_only: live Level 3 flowsheet of the selected basis and tail_gas; null for tail_gas export, burn_on_site and recycle_fixed; did not move for p_abs_bar, w_mea, ihx_approach_k or eta_power in the variant solves
follows_controls.design_point_only: M6 column model at its Case B design point; null as soon as w_mea, lean_loading, capture_target, p_abs_bar or p_strip_bar moves, or the basis or tail_gas changes
follows_controls.no: precomputed results row; label it Precomputed on screen

conventions.units: reply unit C prints as degC; unit - is a fraction and prints as a percentage through panels.js fmtValue(); K to degC is the only other conversion any step needs. Decimals follow panels.js DECIMALS.
conventions.default_value: value at the default inputs, for testing only; never typed into the page

global_rules: Every number on screen is read from the reply path, registry path or results row named here at render time. A null value prints n/a with the matching engine_fields_missing reason.
Moving dashes show the flow direction only. Every stream animates at one fixed screen speed, and a line under the caption says that the motion does not show flow speed.

Anything drawn to explain physics without engine data carries an on-screen Illustration tag: the fission overlay of step 1, reaction equations, the ship and store icons of step 11 and any added heat arrows.

Stream rows of data/streams.json come from the Level 3 flowsheet and the reply comes from the anchored port. Their carbon lines disagree (for example S16 carries 93.9 kmol/h of CO2 against 116.9 kmol/h of burned carbon in the reply, the failed carbon gate of the cryogenic panel), so the tour takes flows and carbon from the reply and uses stream rows only for temperature and pressure, each tagged Precomputed.
When the reply status is not_converged the tour reads state.lastOk and shows the existing Last converged result tag.
On a new reply (onResult hook) the current step re-renders its numbers without moving focus.
Scenario guard: when inputs.tail_gas is not recycle, or inputs.basis is case_a, each step uses its scenario_branches text, because the drawing shows the Case B recycle plant only.
On the site SMR means steam methane reforming only; captions say reformer where they can.

controls.placement: a Tour toolbar outside the svg, in the .pfd-pick row above #pfd-mount, so it stays visible at phone width while the drawing scrolls sideways
controls.caption_region: one div with aria-live=polite outside the scroller, holding the step title, Step n of 13, the caption, the numbers and the tags; set #pfd-panel aria-live to off while the tour runs so the panel does not announce at the same time
controls.focus: Start moves focus to the step title; Exit, or Escape, ends the tour and returns focus to the Start button. Escape closes an open stream tip first, because pfd.js already handles Escape on document for the tip.
controls.keys: the tour adds no global arrow keys; the unit arrow keys of pfd.js keep working
controls.camera: each step calls the existing reveal(unitId) for its first highlighted unit; reveal() uses behavior smooth today and must use auto under prefers-reduced-motion
controls.reduced_motion: no moving dashes, no autoplay, no smooth scroll; the highlighted lines thicken and keep their drawn arrowheads, and the user steps with the buttons
controls.contrast: caption text and tags at 4.5:1 or better on their background

steps.title: Fission heat in the HTGR core
caption: Inside the reactor core, uranium in TRISO fuel particles splits when it absorbs a neutron, and the graphite around the fuel slows the new neutrons so the chain reaction carries on.
The fission energy heats the graphite, and helium passing through the core carries that heat out at {rot} degC.
The reactor is rated at {rating} MWth and runs at the {output} MWth this plant needs, so {surplus} MWth is held as margin.

numbers.label: Helium pressure
numbers.note: assumed; optional

numbers.label: Feasibility
numbers.default_value: Feasible: the 210.0 MWth rating covers the 178.5 MWth the process needs, with 31.5 MWth to spare
numbers.note: engine text; show as is when feasibility.feasible is false

illustration: Overlay inside the core outline (the pp-core path, x 102 to 208, y 380 to 600): TRISO particles in a graphite matrix, a neutron striking a uranium nucleus that splits into two fragments and releases new neutrons, and heat passing to the helium. Tag: Illustration, the engine models the reactor as a heat source and holds no fuel, neutron or core temperature data.
No numerals in the overlay: no MeV, no neutron count, no isotope mass number, since none of them is an engine value.
The flow direction of helium inside the vessel (in at the top nozzle, out at the side outlet) is the drawing's, and the engine does not model it.

steps_without_engine_numbers: Step 1, fission: the engine treats the reactor as a heat source. It has no fission rate, neutron flux, fuel loading, enrichment, burnup, power density, core or fuel temperature, and nothing on TRISO or graphite. Only heat (MWth), the outlet temperature and helium data exist, so the fission picture is illustration only.

Step 11, ship and storage: no voyage, liquefaction, shipping, storage site or injection model. Only the tariff (inputs.ts_s_t), the charge (units.co2_storage.results.ts_cost) and the assumed fuel burden exist; CO2 pressure and temperature come from the precomputed S20 row.
Step 9, burner and stack: no unit or field for the burner of the nitrogen-rich cut; the residual CO2 (kpi.co2_atm_t_y) and the precomputed S15 and S16 rows are all there is.
Step 2, primary return temperature: no live field. T_CIRC_PRIM_K is a registry constant (764 K) that did not move with ihx_approach_k; P1 to P4 and H1, H2 have no stream rows at all.
Step 4, steam feed: no steam flow or steam to carbon ratio in the reply (s_c is a dropped control); the S02 row is precomputed.
Step 5, HPS-GEN1: the boiler between reformer and shift has no reply field; Q_HPS-GEN1 exists only in Integrated_Energy_Balance.csv run FS_B_REC_F.
Step 10, reboiler steam: the reply gives heat in MW and no steam flow; the rich/lean, lean cooler and condenser duties exist only at the M6 design point and belong to that model's own reboiler duty.
